body:
# Independent audit of tight-row corner truncation

Source audited: `candidate bb526889825517af`.
Result: PASS in its stated ordinary-simplex, strict-incidence, sufficiently
small actual truncation scope. No repair is required.

## Actual-body and measure checks

At every original vertex all source-cap margins are nonzero. A sufficiently
small corner homothetic to the original simplex therefore lies wholly in
its own cap and strictly outside every other cap, and is disjoint from all
source cutting hyperplanes. Cutting by a plane parallel to the opposite
facet preserves convexity and the source in the interior. If the corner's
linear scale is t, its lost volume is t^d k. Thus lost volume E is a valid
positive continuous parameter with an interval of attainable values; it is
not necessary, and would be incorrect, to use the nonzero derivative of
lost volume with respect to t at zero for d>1.

The identities k(E)=k-E, Q_j(E)=Q_j-E and unchanged other cap volumes and
all sections are exact. Section normalization is unchanged because no
cutting section meets the removed corner. Positivity of all quantities in
the displayed logarithmic derivatives persists for small E.

## Derivative and constants

Write p=d/(d-1). The proved joint-row equality characterization implies
f_i=x and every other f_l=z with x+(d-1)z^p=d. The gradient has entry 1 at i
and z^(1/(d-1)) elsewhere, so its Euler pairing is

    C=x+d z^p=(d^2-x)/(d-1).

Differentiation of the actual data gives

    f_l'/f_l=-1/(d k)+1/(sigma_j M)
                   -((d-1)/d) 1_(l=j)/Q_j.

With T=d k/(sigma_j M) one has f_j=T(Q_j/k)^((d-1)/d).
Eliminating Q_j/k therefore gives exactly the two source formulae:

    d k Phi_i'=-C+CT-(d-1)x^(-1/(d-1))T^p     (j=i),
    d k Phi_i'=-C+CT-(d-1)T^p                 (j!=i).

For the second expression the gradient factor z^(1/(d-1)) cancels the
same power of f_j=z; no missing z factor remains.

## Strict signs for all dimensions

The respective negatives have unique minima

    C-x(C/d)^d,        C-(C/d)^d.

The stationary T values are x(C/d)^(d-1) and (C/d)^(d-1), respectively.
For the first minimum, differentiating log[x C^(d-1)] gives 1/x-1/C>0,
because C-x=d(d-x)/(d-1)>0. Its limiting value at x=d is d^d, so the
minimum is positive for every actual x in (0,d).

For the second, d<C<d^2/(d-1), hence
(C/d)^(d-1)<(1+1/(d-1))^(d-1)<=d. The final weak bound follows directly
by expanding the binomial: each coefficient divided by the matching
power of d-1 is at most 1, and there are d terms. The strict preceding
inequality also covers d=2, where the binomial bound itself is equality.
Thus its minimum is positive as well.

The planar discriminants in the source agree with these formulae: at
the selected corner, after writing T=x sqrt(k/Q_i), the positive numerator
is (4-x)+x a^2-x(4-x)a with discriminant
-x(4-x)(x-2)^2; at another corner it is
T^2-(4-x)T+(4-x), with discriminant -x(4-x).

## Scope and conclusion

A negative derivative with respect to attained E gives a one-sided interval
of strict improvement for each selected tight row. There are finitely many
rows. Other initially strict rows remain strict by continuity, and any
additional tight row has the same negative-derivative proof. Therefore all
rows are strict after a sufficiently small corner truncation.

This conclusion concerns this actual family of truncated simplices. It
makes no assertion about finite truncations, general-body localization,
uniform neighborhoods under arbitrary changes, or mixed-fiber compatibility.
The companion exact checker is `supporting computation verify_tight_row_corner_truncation_audit_defect_transport.py`.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
